findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

Upon arrival food handling had begun as part of the kitchen start-up operations and a sanitizer had not been prepared for use. The PIC was asked about the situation and prepared a bucket to correct. Ensure that a sanitizer has been prepared and is available, at effective concentration, at all times that food handling and handling of food contact surfaces are taking place.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

The rubber seal on the front side of the chest freezer in the baking room is observed with black mold growth beginning. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. The location was cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that the non-food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

The PIC for this facility currently has an expired CFPM. They are aware and have scheduled for a class next month. The normal kitchen manager is out because of and eye surgery at this time. No other CFPMs are available during this inspection. Hand outs were given for the known CFPM courses in the area during this inspection. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs to cover all shifts at the facility.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

Spatulas are observed store between the pipe and the wall above the three part sink. This is not an easily cleanable surface and so is a poor location to store food contact items. The spatulas were moved to dish for cleaning to correct the immediate violation. Per the PIC the utensils will go back to being stored in tubs prior to use.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Test strips were not available for the sanitizer used in this facility at the beginning of this inspection. The PIC indicated that the roll got wet recently and had not been replaced yet. A small amount were acquired during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that test strips are always available for the sanitizers used in the facility.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Facility was found to be operating outside of its medium risk permit by cooling and reheating foods. Improper cooling time/temperature and cooling methods were observed as well. Inspector will follow up to see that facility is operating within permit and, if upgraded, further discuss cooling methods.
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  [Pf]

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.comment: Facility is operating outside of their permit by cooling and reheating cheese sauce and two types of soup (actions not allowed under a Class II Medium Risk permit). Cease cooling and reheating or upgrade to a Class I High Risk permit. CORRECTED- Previously cooled foods in the facility may not be served as cooling violations were also observed during this inspection. Foods will be voluntarily discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-201.11 (A) FOOD shall be obtained from sources that comply with LAW. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
Container of cheese sauce observed to be 125F (probed) at 4:30. Per PIC, cheese sauce began cooling at 2PM. Cheese sauce did not cool to from 135 to 70 in two hours. CORRECTED- Cheese sauce was voluntarily discarded. Discussed cooling time & temperatures as well as cooling methods. Additional education will be provided if facility decides to upgrade permit and continue cooling/reheating.
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
An open gallon of milk was observed without date marking indicating the date it was opened. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, who labeled milk with the date it was opened. Label foods and use or discard within 7 days of opening.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. [Pf]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Unlabeled spray bottle of clear liquid observed in a bucket of other chemicals in the kitchen. PIC was unsure what was in the container, opened and smelled it, and determined it to be water. She indicated that the bucket is the janitor’s supplies. CORRECTED- Spray bottle was labeled to indicate contents. Ensure chemicals (or what may be mistaken for chemicals) are labeled to indicate contents and avoid confusion.
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Cheese sauce observed cooling in the kitchen cooler, covered and with no other additional cooling methods used. Cheese sauce had not met the time/temperature benchmarks. Cheese sauce was voluntarily discarded. Discussed cooling methods. Inspector will follow up to verify that cooling has ceased, or to provide additional education if cooling will continue.
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. [Pf]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Facility does not have employee health documentation on file. CORRECTED— Inspector provided Food Employee Reporting Agreement. Keep signed copies on file for each food employee.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  [Pf]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
Facility does not have a written vomit/diarrhea clean up policy on file. CORRECTED— Inspector provided a vomit/diarrhea clean up policy. Post or keep on file where staff know to find it in case of vomit/diarrhea events.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment: Observed employee beverage in an uncovered cup in the food preparation area. Provide a lid and straw for beverage cups. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Lid and straw were provided.
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11 (A) Except as specified in ¶ (B) of this section, an EMPLOYEE shall eat, drink, or use any form of tobacco only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; or other items needing protection can not result. (C)

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: Clean utensils stored incorrectly in a wooden knife block. Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted.

4-903.11 (A) Except as specified in ¶ (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other
contamination. (C)

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Turkey (deli) is observed to be in the bottom of the prep unit at 46F. The turkey was discarded. Foods reading 43F (beef patties) and 42F (deli ham) were moved to a working unit. Do not use this unit until it is functioning and able to maintain food at 41F or below. 750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: White vents and ceiling tiles in front and above the hood vent are soiled with dust. Clean and maintain clean. 750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed hot dogs and chicken patties opened and without a date mark. Manager stated that the hot dogs were opened 2 days ago and the chicken was opened yesterday. Manager was allowed to date mark the foods. Ensure that any RTE, PHFs that are opened are date marked, then used or discarded within 7 days. 
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Observed a yellowish liquid in a spray bottle without a label. Manager stated it was bleach water. Ensure that when chemicals are placed into spray bottles that they are labeled. This will decrease the chances of accidental cross-contamination with it or misuse of the chemical. Manager labeled the chemical during the inspection. 
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed a 5 gallon container of chili in the cooler that was probed at a temperature of 55F. The food was cooked yesterday the employee stated. Food should follow the guidelines listed below. Additional measures should be taken to increase cooling effectiveness: 1) Shallow pans. 2) Ice Baths. 3) Placement in Freezers to assist in reaching 41F in a quick, effective manner. Chili was discarded during the inspection. 
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed a stack of styrofoam containers improperly stored.  Store inverted or covered.  Corrected:  The containers were inverted.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed an accumulation of soil on the floor under the steam table at the wall.  Clean the floor and maintain clean.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed shelving and other equipment stored haphazardly around the old oven.  Store in an organized manner.
750-1350c Only articles necessary for the operation and maintenance of the food service establishment shall be stored on the premises.  Remove all unnecessary items.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed several cooked and cooled items including mashed potatoes, green beans and gravy without a proper label.  Label with the time and date, any potentially hazardous food that you prepare.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed gravy, green beans, mashed potatoes, etc. in a cooler without a proper label.  Label with the date prepared and use, sell or discard within seven days.  Corrected.  Cory will label the food containers with the date of preparation.  Most were made yesterday.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Did not observe a thermometer in the chest freezer in the kitchen or the Frigidaire reach in cooler.  Provide conspicuously located thermometers.
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1. Observed debris in the container holding scoops and 2. mildew inside the top ledge of the ice maker.  Clean and sanitize the container and scoops and inside the ice maker.
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed an accumulation of soil in the drawer containing pot holders.  Clean the drawer.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed two containers of utensils improperly stored. Store the utensils so that the handles are extended.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed both hand sinks to be soiled.  Clean the hand sinks and maintain clean.
750-1120 Lavatories, soap dispensers, hand drying devices and all related fixtures Shall be clean and in good repair.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed several floor tiles in the baking room that are in disrepair.  Replace the tile.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Absence of labels on several items in upright cooler.  Items were used previous day in an ice bath, due to prep cooler not working and another one is on order, and the labels came off in ice bath.  Kitchen manager, Julia, has been present all week and is aware of when each food item was prepared and will replace all labels with the appropriate date.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed a flat carton of eggs to be stored on top of containers of condiments in the upright cooler in the kitchen.  The eggs were moved to the proper location during inspection. Proper meat and egg placement was discussed with the kitchen manager during inspection and a "Proper Placement" sheet was given.  *Violation Corrected*
750-130(d)  All raw meat shall be properly stored, store in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed a couple bags of soda syrup that have come out of the soda boxes and are lying on the floor.  Move soda syrup bags off the floor at least 6 inches.
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1. bottom of cart storing utensils by the 3 compartment sink  2. cart storing the trays by the 3 compartment sink  3. outside of both toasters  4. racks/shelves in the Tropicana cooler in kitchen (if rusty, scrape off rust and re-paint/re-seal, so that no rust is present and it is smooth and easily cleanable)
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed an area of the floor in the back bakery area, by the chest freezer, to be in disrepair.  Repair the floor so that it is smooth and easily cleanable.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the door on the Tropicana cooler to not close properly. The staff is aware of this and ordered a new part to fix the door, so it closes properly.  It is being held closed with velcro and tape and the temperature is 41 degrees F or below.
Observed the gasket on the chest freezer in the front kitchen area to be in disrepair and inside part of the lid to be cracked, allowing insulation to be visible on this same chest freezer.  Repair this gasket and inside plastic piece of the lid, so that it is smooth and easily cleanable and allows the freezer to seal properly.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b: Observed a small amount of mold growth on the inside, plastic piece of the ice machine.  Clean and sanitize this inside, plastic piece of the ice machine to prevent mold growth and protect ice from contamination.
